definitions.gloss: enrollment fee; entrance fee paid upon admission to a school
definitions.explanation: A one-time fee paid when entering a school, university, or other educational institution in Japan. This is separate from tuition and is typically non-refundable.

examples.japanese: {入学金|にゅうがくきん}を{納|おさ}める。
{入学金|にゅうがくきん}は{三十万円|さんじゅうまんえん}だった。
{私立|しりつ}{大学|だいがく}の{入学金|にゅうがくきん}は{国立|こくりつ}より{高|たか}いことが{多|おお}い。
examples.english: The enrollment fee for private universities is often higher than for national universities.

notes:
Composed of {入学|にゅうがく} (enrollment/admission) and {金|きん} (money/fee). In the Japanese education system, {入学金|にゅうがくきん} is a standard one-time payment required upon acceptance to a school, separate from {授業料|じゅぎょうりょう} (tuition). It is typically non-refundable, even if the student decides not to attend.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {入学金|にゅうがくきん}を{払|はら}う: to pay the entrance fee
- {入学金|にゅうがくきん}を{納|おさ}める: to pay/submit the entrance fee (formal)
- {入学金|にゅうがくきん}{免除|めんじょ}: exemption from the entrance fee
- {入学金|にゅうがくきん}の{返還|へんかん}: refund of the entrance fee

RELATED WORDS:
- {授業料|じゅぎょうりょう}: tuition fees — the recurring cost of attending classes
- {学費|がくひ}: school expenses — a broader term covering all educational costs
- {受験料|じゅけんりょう}: examination fee — paid to take an entrance exam
